html:
SMTO-CFG-0036 — SMTO wasn't told which settings file to use

GUID: db01795c-29da-4e99-84ae-fb5506cb59fa
Slug: config-explicit-app-config-not-found-pass-config
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to start with a specific settings file, but no file location was given, so it stopped. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you use a custom settings file, start SMTO with ./startup.sh --config followed by the file's full path. This names the file SMTO should load, which is what the message asks for.
  2. If you don't use a custom settings file, start SMTO the usual way with ./startup.sh and no --config option. Without a named file, SMTO reads config.yaml from its own folder, or uses its built-in settings when there is none.
  3. If SMTO is started by a script or service someone else set up, ask them to set AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH to the settings file's full path. That setting tells SMTO where the file is when it isn't started by hand.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message and send it, with how you start SMTO, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change other startup options to work around it; they don't decide which settings file is used.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap configuration loading reported that an explicit application configuration file is required but no path was supplied through --config or AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH.

What this means

  • The missing-config formatter has a no-path variant, but current normal loading accepts an absent implicit config.yaml and returns typed defaults. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • The missing-config formatter has a no-path variant, but current normal loading accepts an absent implicit config.yaml and returns typed defaults.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual caller's explicit-config requirement; this retained variant does not prove that ordinary startup requires a file.

How to fix it

  • Find the caller that formats this message without a path; the current load_app_config falls back to config.yaml in the working directory, or typed defaults, when no explicit path is set. Pass --config with an existing file or set AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH only when that startup path really requires one; otherwise rely on the implicit config.yaml or defaults.
  • Check the calling startup path and provide an explicit file only when that path requires one.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual caller uses an intended explicit file or supported typed defaults.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
